label.purpose: Functional micro-labels: stack-group headers, eyebrows, tags.

shadows.name: cta-hover
shadows.purpose: Primary portfolio CTA hover; only place the accent tints a shadow.

motion.name: state-transition
motion.purpose: Color/border/background/shadow/transform transitions on hover and focus. Not a named easing curve today — see audit note on adopting ease-out-quart/expo.

components.name: Primary Button
components.description: Inverted ink-on-paper pill, the single most important action per view.
components.css: .ds-btn-primary { background: var(--text); color: var(--bg); border: 1px solid var(--text); border-radius: 999px; padding: 0.48rem 0.9rem; min-height: 2.35rem; font-size: 0.875rem; font-weight: 650; transition: color 0.2s, border-color 0.2s, background 0.2s; } .ds-btn-primary:hover { background: var(--text-secondary); } .ds-btn-primary:focus-visible { outline: 2px solid var(--accent); outline-offset: 2px; }

components.name: Secondary Button
components.description: Hairline ghost pill for every action that isn't the single primary one.
components.css: .ds-btn-secondary { background: var(--card-bg); color: var(--text); border: 1px solid var(--border); border-radius: 999px; padding: 0.48rem 0.9rem; min-height: 2.35rem; font-size: 0.875rem; font-weight: 650; transition: color 0.2s, border-color 0.2s, background 0.2s; } .ds-btn-secondary:hover { background: var(--card-hover); border-color: var(--text-secondary); } .ds-btn-secondary:focus-visible { outline: 2px solid var(--accent); outline-offset: 2px; }

components.name: Card
components.description: Flat-at-rest container; shadow and lift only on hover.
components.html:
Post title

Short description of the post.
components.css: .ds-card { display: block; padding: 0.9rem 1rem; border: 1px solid var(--border); border-radius: 8px; background: var(--card-bg); transition: border-color 0.2s, box-shadow 0.2s, transform 0.2s; } .ds-card:hover { border-color: color-mix(in srgb, var(--accent) 36%, var(--border)); box-shadow: 0 14px 34px color-mix(in srgb, #000 8%, transparent); transform: translateY(-1px); }

components.name: Badge
components.description: Accent-bordered tag/category pill; accent tints the border only, never the fill.
components.css: .ds-badge { display: inline-flex; align-items: center; padding: 0.2rem 0.6rem; border: 1px solid color-mix(in srgb, var(--accent) 24%, var(--border)); border-radius: 999px; background: var(--card-bg); color: var(--text-secondary); font-size: 0.7rem; font-weight: 700; }

components.name: Icon Hit Target
components.description: Small visual icon (20-24px) wrapped to a larger invisible clickable box via negative margin, so the icon's footprint in layout is unchanged but the tap target grows.
components.css: .ds-icon-target { display: inline-flex; align-items: center; justify-content: center; width: 32px; height: 32px; margin: -6px; color: var(--text-secondary); }

narrative.overview: The site reads like a well-kept engineering notebook: near-black ink on near-white paper, hairline rules instead of decoration, and exactly one brand accent color allowed to speak. Nothing performs confidence — the restraint is the confidence. Every surface is flat at rest; the only signal that something is interactive is a hairline border, a soft shadow on hover, and a 1px lift. This system explicitly rejects the generic SaaS landing page (no gradient heroes, no hero-metric blocks, no eyebrow kickers dressing up every section) and the over-designed agency portfolio (no scroll-jacking, no oversized type stunts that outshine the work being shown). The work and the writing are the product; the chrome should recede.
keyCharacteristics: Monochrome ink/paper base with a single signal-blue brand accent, never more
Flat surfaces; shadow and lift exist only as hover feedback, never as default elevation
Full-pill (999px) buttons and badges; 8px cards; hairline 1px borders everywhere else
One typeface (Inter) carrying every register from hero display to body copy
Light/dark are full token-for-token mirrors, not an afterthought
Icon-only controls keep a small visual size but a 32-44px clickable hit area

rules.name: The One Signal Rule
rules.body: Signal Blue is the only chromatic brand color anywhere in the UI. If a second brand accent is ever needed, that's a sign the design has drifted toward a marketing site — stop and reconsider before adding it.

rules.name: The Borrowed Brand Rule
rules.body: Icons linking to a named external service (RSS, GitHub, LinkedIn, GitLab, StackOverflow, Telegram, email) may reveal that service's own canonical brand color on hover/focus. This is a recognition aid for a third-party identity, not a second site accent, and does not violate the One Signal Rule. It must still clear 3:1 contrast against the surface it sits on.

rules.name: The Single-Family Rule
rules.body: Inter is the only typeface in the system. Don't introduce a second family for contrast — vary weight and size instead.

rules.name: The Flat-By-Default Rule
rules.body: No element carries a shadow at rest. A shadow only appears as a transition response to :hover or an open/active state.

dos: Do keep Signal Blue as the only chromatic brand accent; everything else is ink/paper/hairline.
Do keep buttons and badges full-pill (999px); keep cards at 8-12px depending on size.
Do keep shadows flat-at-rest, hover-triggered only.
Do keep the single Inter family; differentiate via weight and size, not a second font.
Do keep prose containers narrow (640-680px) and hero h1 capped at 13ch for balanced wrapping.
Do keep icon-only controls at a 32-44px clickable hit area even when the visual icon stays small.
Do let an external-service icon reveal its own brand color on hover/focus per the Borrowed Brand Rule.
donts: Don't introduce a generic SaaS landing page move: gradient heroes, hero-metric blocks, or a tiny uppercase eyebrow above every section.
Don't add agency-portfolio flourishes: scroll-jacking, oversized type stunts, or motion that competes with the work being shown.
Don't use border-left/border-right colored accent stripes on cards or list items, except a blog-post blockquote (an editorial convention, not the dashboard-card tell).

Don't add a second brand accent color; route any new emphasis case through Signal Blue, weight, or size instead. Borrowed third-party brand colors on external-service icons are the one sanctioned exception.
Don't give a card or button a resting shadow - shadows only respond to :hover/:focus.
Don't color error text decoratively - the error token is reserved for form-validation failures only.
